rationale: Corrected discriminator for the snapshot-trigger defect's install-snapshot route, after the previous construction was refuted because AddVoter and the following replication refilled the follower's log above the installed snapshot. The harness now catches the new voter up, isolates it, applies three more commands on the leader and takes a fresh snapshot (compacting the leader's log up to that index with TrailingLogs=0), then reconnects so the follower must install a snapshot whose index is above its own remaining log. Native construction feedback with these fixed inputs gave a decisive positive with otherwise default follower settings: the leader's snapshot while the target was isolated was index 8, the target then installed that snapshot (installed_index=8, snapshot_index=8) while its log store's last index was 5, so store_emptied=true and should_snapshot=true. That is exactly the underflow the source reading predicts, reached through a normal follower catch-up event rather than a caller-chosen trailing count. This submission records the fixed experiment for controller execution; the measured interpretation is left for the retained receipt.

scope.description: One process: two real raft instances bootstrapped with TrailingLogs=0 plus a third fresh instance merged into the same transport set. The leader applies an entry, takes a snapshot, applies another, then adds the fresh node with AddVoter and lets it catch up for 500ms. The new voter is then isolated at the transport level, the leader applies three more commands and takes a second snapshot (its own log compacted up to that index), the transport is reconnected, and the harness waits until the isolated node's cached snapshot index reaches the leader's snapshot index before sampling, after a further 150ms, its log store last index, snapshot index, applied index, commit index, store_emptied and shouldSnapshot.

experiment.prefix: MakeCluster(2, t, conf) with conf.TrailingLogs=0 supplies the two Voters and the leader; MakeClusterNoBootstrap(1, t, nil) supplies the third instance with an empty log, default trailing count and default threshold, which is the node whose verdict is measured. Merge plus FullyConnect wire the transports; cluster.Disconnect on the third node's address isolates it in both directions and FullyConnect restores it, so the leader cannot reach it while it snapshots and compacts, and after reconnection the leader's replication for that peer must fall back to sending its latest snapshot (the existing replicateTo path that switches to SEND_SNAP when the previous log entry is unavailable). No production logic is modified; the sampling is of the third node's own runtime state, and the wait is on the observed snapshot index rather than a fixed delay.
experiment.revision_reason: The previous construction never left the follower below its snapshot index because AddVoter appended a configuration entry above the installed snapshot and replication kept the log filled. This revision isolates the added voter before taking the leader's snapshot, so after reconnection the follower must install a snapshot at an index above whatever stale log entries it still holds, which is the state the source reading predicts and the previous run could not reach.
